text.content:
Veterans who started out protecting the neighborhood. One of the Old Three.

Turf: Santo Domingo (Rancho Coronado and Arroyo), the Heywood edges, Westbrook's west slope
Known for: Rifles, shotguns and legacy military gear; extortion, theft and drugs sold as protection
Leadership: "General" Rick Morton
Allies & rivals: At war with the Valentinos along the Heywood–Arroyo line. Patron of the DeadWoods
Hangouts: The Armory (#80), the Forlorn Hope (#79), Tripple Xtreme (#47)

6th Street began as a militia of veterans who protected their neighborhoods when nobody else would. It had veterans in every precinct and Militech's sympathy, and it was never on the Purge List. The 2050s and '60s were hard on it: desperate for resources, it gave up its founding principles and became no better than the gangs it was founded to fight.

Today 6th Street uses its position in Santo Domingo for extortion, theft and drugs, and calls it protection. In Rancho Coronado its patrols knock on doors on the first of the month; pay and you're protected, don't and your house has accidents. The "General" keeps up the military theater of ranks, drills and a code nobody follows, under old American flags, surplus camo and unit patches from forgotten wars.

The War with the Valentinos

In 2070 Arasaka bought the idle Arroyo plants around its Industrial Park, and 6th Street lost the protection money. It started a turf war with the Valentinos to make up for it. Last year the war cost both sides more bodies than the Unification War did.

Edgerunner's Handbook p.25; Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.02, 04, 11
